==Problem==

The midpoints of the four sides of a rectangle are <imath>(-3,0), (2,0), (5,4),</imath> and <imath>(0,4).</imath> What is the
area of the rectangle? 

<imath>\textbf{(A) } 20 \qquad \textbf{(B) } 25 \qquad \textbf{(C) } 40 \qquad \textbf{(D) } 50 \qquad \textbf{(E) } 80</imath>

==Solution 1==

The midpoints of the four sides of every rectangle are the vertices of a rhombus whose area is half the area of the rectangle: Note that the diagonals of the rhombus have the same lengths as the sides of the rectangle.

Let <imath>A=(-3,0), B=(2,0), C=(5,4),</imath> and <imath>D=(0,4).</imath> Note that <imath>A,B,C,</imath> and <imath>D</imath> are the vertices of a rhombus whose diagonals have lengths <imath>AC=4\sqrt{5}</imath> and <imath>BD=2\sqrt{5}.</imath> It follows that the dimensions of the rectangle are <imath>4\sqrt{5}</imath> and <imath>2\sqrt{5},</imath> so the area of the rectangle is <imath>4\sqrt{5}\cdot2\sqrt{5}=\boxed{\textbf{(C) } 40}.</imath>

~MRENTHUSIASM

==Solution 2==

If a rectangle has area <imath>K,</imath> then the area of the quadrilateral formed by its midpoints is <imath>\frac{K}{2}.</imath>

Define points <imath>A,B,C,</imath> and <imath>D</imath> as Solution 1 does. Since <imath>A,B,C,</imath> and <imath>D</imath> are the midpoints of the rectangle, the rectangle's area is <imath>2[ABCD].</imath> Now, note that <imath>ABCD</imath> is a parallelogram since <imath>AB=CD</imath> and <imath>\overline{AB}\parallel\overline{CD}.</imath> As the parallelogram's height from <imath>D</imath> to <imath>\overline{AB}</imath> is <imath>4</imath> and <imath>AB=5,</imath> its area is <imath>4\cdot5=20.</imath> Therefore, the area of the rectangle is <imath>20\cdot2=\boxed{\textbf{(C) } 40}.</imath>

~Fruitz
==Solution 3==

Graph paper is not permitted on the AMC 8. Still, blank scratch paper is provided, and with that, you can draw a makeshift coordinate plane and "graph" some dots. It doesn't have to be very exact, but do make reasonable estimates on the locations of the points. Once you graph the dots and look around, it becomes apparent that the only rectangle that would make sense would be if the length were from (-3,0) to (5,4), and the width would have to be from (0,4) to (2,0). With that in mind, use the distance formula to solve for the length and width. The distance formula is as follows:

<imath>d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}</imath>


Simply put the coordinates into the formula to get the distance between the two points. Using the formula, the length is <imath>\sqrt{80}</imath>, and the width is <imath>\sqrt{20}</imath>. Now, multiply the length and width together to get <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C) } 40}.</imath> ~Evžen D.
